title: Swirled Chocolate Babka
summary: A richly swirled chocolate loaf with a glossy syrup glaze, twisted to show off ribbons of dark chocolate filling in every slice.
equipment: 2 x 900 g (23 x 13 cm) loaf tins lined with baking paper

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, add the milk, eggs, alcohol-free vanilla extract and orange zest, and knead for 5 minutes. Add the butter a little at a time and knead for a further 6-8 minutes until the dough is smooth and elastic. Cover and chill overnight; the cold rest firms this soft, buttery dough so it's easier to roll thinly later.

steps.title: Make the chocolate filling
steps.text: Melt the chocolate and butter together over low heat, stirring until smooth, then beat in the icing sugar and cocoa powder. Leave it to cool until thick enough to spread without running - a little patience here stops the filling oozing out once the dough is rolled and twisted.

steps.title: Roll and fill
steps.text: Halve the cold dough and roll each piece out to 40 x 28cm. Spread each with half the chocolate filling, leaving a 1cm border clear, then roll up tightly from the long side into a log and chill both logs for 15 minutes to firm up.

steps.title: Twist and prove
steps.text: Cut each log in half lengthways to expose the chocolate swirl, lay the two halves cut-side up next to each other, twist them over one another and tuck in the ends before setting each twist into its tin. Cover and leave to prove for 1½-2 hours, until the dough has risen about 2cm above the rim of the tin.

steps.title: Bake until set
steps.text: At 180°C (160°C fan), bake for 35-40 minutes, covering with foil if the top browns too fast. The loaves are done when a skewer comes out free of raw dough and the centre reads 88-93°C, telling you the rich, buttery crumb is cooked through without drying out.

steps.title: Glaze and cool
steps.text: Boil the sugar and water together for 1 minute to make a thin syrup, then brush it generously over the hot loaves straight from the oven - this is what gives babka its glossy finish. Cool the loaves in their tins for 20 minutes before turning out onto the wire rack to finish cooling.

tips: Chill the filling until it's thick and spreadable, not runny - a loose filling squeezes out during twisting and leaves bald patches.
Chill the rolled logs before cutting and twisting, as firmer dough holds its swirl much better than warm, soft dough.
Brush the syrup on while the loaves are still hot straight from the oven, since the warm crumb soaks it in rather than letting it pool on top.
Cover the loaves with foil partway through baking if they're browning before the centre is cooked, so the crust doesn't turn bitter.
Let the loaves cool in the tin briefly before turning out, as babka is fragile and warm bread tears easily.
storage: Store the cooled babka airtight at room temperature for up to 2 days, or freeze for up to 1 month. Warm briefly in a low oven before serving if you'd like it piping hot again. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
